candidate.title: SMDB
candidate.scope: Single-molecule droplet barcoding (SMDB), at the architecture level of the assigned Illumina SMDB row, clarified by the full text of Lan et al., Nature Communications 7:11784 (2016), DOI 10.1038/ncomms11784. The target is individual DNA template molecules, represented by barcoded fragments for short-read sequencing; this is not a cell-identity or RNA readout. The complete row shows DNA templates, single-template encapsulation, amplification, fragmentation, droplet barcoding, and pooling for library preparation. The yellow DNA motif beside the expanded method name is descriptive: no arrow connects it as another operation. Dip-C above, the Integrated Techniques heading, and SIDR below are neighboring catalogue content, with no material route into SMDB. The SMDB row has no alternative target workflow or retained branch. Paper-supported chemistry clarifies the depicted operations; unshown device construction, barcode production, cleanup internals, sequencing, and computation are not added as workflow operations.

operations.label: Single template encapsulation
operations.description: Partitions DNA template molecules from solution into separate droplets, producing the occupied and empty droplet compartments shown. The paper clarifies statistical loading, with most droplets containing zero or one template.
operations.mechanism: Microfluidic encapsulation of DNA templates in aqueous droplets; no concentration or execution conditions are implied by the drawing.
operations.information_effect: Physical separation establishes the initial template-to-compartment association. An occupied droplet is intended to represent one DNA template, not one cell.

operations.label: Template amplification
operations.description: Clonally amplifies the DNA template within each occupied droplet, increasing the DNA copy number while retaining compartmental separation.
operations.mechanism: In-droplet clonal amplification; the primary Figure 2a caption names PCR or MDA. These are components of the amplification block, not separate target workflows in this card.
operations.information_effect: Multiple copies provide repeated sequence coverage of the original template after fragmentation; compartmentalization retains their common origin.

evidence.quote: Inside droplets, PCR or MDA is used to clonally amplify the single template.

operations.label: Template fragmentation
operations.description: Converts the amplified DNA copies to shorter DNA fragments within droplets. The primary paper resolves the generic fragmentation icon as fragmentation accompanied by adaptor addition.
operations.mechanism: Tn5 transposase fragments amplified template DNA and adds short adaptor sequences while compartmentalization is maintained.
operations.information_effect: Fragments from an amplified template remain grouped physically in its droplet. The newly attached adaptor sequences provide the interface used for subsequent barcode attachment.

evidence.locator: b00115, Figure 2b caption
evidence.quote: The transposase reaction inside droplets fragments templates while adding adaptors to each fragment.

operations.label: Barcode every droplet
operations.description: Appends a droplet-associated barcode sequence to the template-derived fragments, represented by common colored ends within each occupied droplet. The source caption is retained, but the primary implementation does not barcode every physical droplet or recover every encapsulated template.
operations.mechanism: Overlap-extension PCR attaches barcode DNA through sequence homology to the adaptors introduced by transposase fragmentation. The paper supplies the barcode-DNA input to this collapsed operation; no separate barcode-generation or device-merging operations are drawn here.
operations.information_effect: Converts physical co-compartmentalization into a sequence tag on the DNA fragments, allowing their common source template to be tracked after mixing. This is an intended template association: empty barcode droplets, co-encapsulation and mistagging prevent universal labeling or perfectly pure barcode groups.

evidence.locator: b00019, Results / Validation of single-molecule barcoding, non-dominant reads
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, we observe a low background of <2% of reads mapping to the non-dominant template in less than half of the barcode clusters, which we attribute to mis-tagging, a phenomenon often observed in barcoded sequence libraries prepared in well plates, and thought to originate from chimeric PCR products generated during library amplification and sequencing29.

operations.label: Pool for library prep
operations.description: Releases and combines the barcoded DNA contents into the mixed DNA material shown for library preparation. The absence of droplet boundaries in the final icon is clarified by the primary paper's emulsion rupture and DNA recovery. The broad library-preparation interface remains broad.
operations.mechanism: Droplet rupture permits recovery and pooling of barcoded fragment DNA; the diagram does not specify the internal sequence of downstream library preparation.
operations.information_effect: Barcode sequences persist on the DNA fragments after compartment boundaries are removed. In the paper-supported readout, short DNA sequence reads are grouped by barcode to recover sequence information for an original template, including consensus or synthetic long sequence reconstruction and linked SNP haplotypes. These are downstream interpretations, not additional operations drawn in this row. A barcode cluster does not guarantee a pure or complete original molecule: co-encapsulation and mistagging can introduce other templates, and amplification/fragmentation biases can leave uneven coverage.

method_scopes.rationale: SMDB is the sole named target of this assigned card and diagram row; its expanded name is an alias, not a separate method. All five drawn operation instances apply to that SMDB route. The Lan et al. full text explicitly names SMDB and supports this same encapsulate-amplify-fragment-barcode workflow. Unshown sequencing and barcode-based interpretation explain the library readout without extending the drawn operation graph.
